Internal hollow cavity of body is called spongocoel which is lined by choanocytes. Choanocytes are flagellated collar cells. 9. Their skeleton is formed of either spongin fibres or silicious spicules or calcareous spicules. 10. They have no alimentary canal and digestion takes place inside the cell (intracellular digestion). 11. Respiratory, excretory and nervous system are absent. Respiration and excretion take place through general body surface. 12. Nervous and sensory cells are not differentiated. Individual cell responds to stimuli. 13. They are hermaphrodite but there always occur cross fertilization. 14. They reproduce asexually by budding, gemmule formation and regeneration. 15. Sexual reproduction takes place by the fusion of sperms and ovum and fertilization is internal. There is holoblastic cleavage of zygote and development is indirect with free swimming ciliated larva called parenchymula or amphiblastula larva. The larva finally settles on a substratum and undergoes metamorphosis to spend sedentary mode of life.

Unique features: primitive multicellular animals, cellular grade of body organization, numerous pores in the body, presence of water canal system, adult form fixed or attached on substratum, internal hollow cavity is spongoecoel, skeleton in the form of calcareous or silicious spicules or spongin fibres, parenchymula or amphiblastula larva Classification Based on the types of skeleton found, following are the classes of porifera:

Class 1: Calcarea (L; calcareous-limy) or calcispongiae i. They have calcareous (made from calcium carbonate) spicules as skeleton which are monaxon, tetraxon and triradiate. ii. Body shape is vase like or cylindrical. iii. They are found in shallow marine water. iv. They are smaller sized and dull coloured sponges. v. They are solitary or colonial.

Example: Sycon (vase sponge), Grantia, leucosolenia, Clathrina Class 2: Hexactinellida (Gr; hex- six; actin-ray) or hyalospongiae (Gr; hyalos- glassy; spongos - sponge) i. They have six rayed silicious (made from silica) spicules as skeleton which are triaxon. ii. They are found in deep marine water. iii. Body shape is like cup and vase. iv. They are moderate sized and commonly called glass rope sponges. v. Most of them are solitary.

Example: Euplectella (venus flower basket), Hyalonema (glass rope sponge), Pheronema (bowl sponge), Farnera etc.

Class 3: Demospongiae (Gr; demos-frame; sponges- sponge) i. They have skeleton in the form of sponging fibres or silicious spicules with sponging fibre or no skeleton. Spicules are never six rayed. ii. They are mostly found in marine water. Few of them are found in fresh water such as Spongila, Ephydatia. iii. Body shape is vase or cup or cushion like. iv. They are more numerous and mostly large sized sponges. v. They are solitary or colonial.

Example: Euspongia (bath sponge), Chalina (mermaids’ sponge), Phyllospongia (leaf sponge), Cliona (boring sponge), etc. 8.2.3 PHYLUM COELENTERATA Leukart created the phylum coelenterata (Gr; koilos-cavity; enteron-intestine) and Hatschek named them as cnidarians. They are commonly called cnidarians or stinging animals as they specialized stinging cells or nematocyst (Cnidoblast or nematoblast) in their body.

General characters
1. They are all aquatic, mostly found in marine water; few of them are found in fresh water such as Hydra.
2. Level of body organization is cell-tissue grade because some cells are aggregated to form tissue and there is no formation of organs and system.
3. They are either solitary or colonial and sedentary; found attached on substratum like rocks stone and hard objects. Some of them are free swimming.

4. They are diploblastic i.e developed from two germ layers. Their body wall consists of outer ectodermal layer and inner endodermal layer of cells with gelationous mesogloea in between. Composition of mesogloea varies which may be either acellular or cellula r with connective tissue.

5. They are acoelomate animals. 6. The shape of the body is hollow tube-like, umbrella- like or large bell-like. 7. The mouth and margin of the bell are surrounded by slender and short tentacles. 8. Tentacles help in capturing and ingestion of food and also in locomotion in some forms.
Stinging cells or cnidoblasts help in paralyzing prey and also in defence.

9. They exhibit unique phenomenon of polymorphism in which main forms or zooids are polyps and medusa. Polyp is the asexual zooid found attached on substratum while medusa is free swimming having role in sexual reproduction.
